Milestone 1: Inventory repository files and status
Goal: Establish the actual repository state before any implementation.
Run inventory commands: `pwd`, `git status --short`, `find . -maxdepth 3 -type f | sort`, `find . -maxdepth 2 -type d | sort`.
Record discovered top-level files/directories in Surprises & Discoveries.
Record whether runtime manifests, source directories, tests, CI, or docs already exist.
Expected result: prints `preflight: ok` after blueprint files and scripts are present.

Recovery instruction: If preflight fails for missing blueprint files, verify the pack is placed at repository root; if it fails for missing tools, record tool absence and continue only if the missing tool is not needed until a later milestone.

Goal: Replace provisional npm/Cargo assumptions only when repository evidence proves a different choice.

Expected result: preflight still passes and COMMANDS.md matches repository evidence.
Recovery instruction: If manifests are absent, keep provisional npm/Cargo assumption, record absence, and do not invent package scripts.

Goal: Identify validation capabilities and missing foundations.
List existing test/lint/build scripts if any.

Expected result: preflight passes; missing runtime commands are documented as placeholders.
Recovery instruction: If directories are absent, record `not present` rather than creating them in EP-000.

Goal: Compare actual repository structure to intended architecture and identify blockers.
Record deviations from intended six runtime layers.
Identify risks: missing manifests, missing tests, missing CI, missing migrations, missing runtime, missing docs.

Expected result: preflight passes and discovery notes are recorded.
Recovery instruction: If architecture cannot be inferred because no runtime exists, record governance-only status and leave proposed architecture intact.

Decision: Use one Rust `SessionActor` per session, a bounded multi-priority event bus, priority-tagged queues, reserved P0/P1 capacity, and backpressure rules.
Alternatives Considered: Single global event loop, UI-owned session state, unbounded async channels.
Consequences: Event contracts and tests must verify priority behavior; optional workers receive derived events only.
Context: WireMudder must start as a blazing-fast traditional MUD client.
Decision: Socket I/O, terminal output, manual command entry, command send, connection health, and emergency stop are sacred P0 operations.
Alternatives Considered: Feature-first AI/renderer integration, terminal through general React state.
Consequences: AI/voice/renderer/memory/telemetry/update/package/help/source indexing must be asynchronous, budgeted, cancelable, degradable, measurable, and isolated.
ADR-0004: Local-First Privacy and Local Only Lockdown
Context: Users own their data and external submission requires consent.
Decision: Privacy modes are disabled, local-only, local-preferred, remote-redacted, and remote-approved; Local Only Lockdown disables remote-capable behavior unless explicitly exited.
Alternatives Considered: Remote-first sync, opt-out telemetry, provider-default AI routing.
Consequences: AI, telemetry, voice, packages, updates, help indexes, and asset fetches require consent gates.
ADR-0005: SQLite, Transcript Chunks, FTS, and Vector Boundary
Context: WireMudder needs searchable local memory and transcript data without blocking gameplay.
Decision: Use SQLite for metadata and search, append-only transcript chunks for raw text, FTS for search, and vector records only for selected facts/summaries.
Alternatives Considered: Store every line in vectors, remote database, flat files only.
Consequences: Persistence writes are async; vector indexing is idle/background; no per-line vector indexing.
